report.summary: Synthesized two cross-file hypotheses: (1) egress screening and worktree allocation both assume a lexical path check is sufficient, but symlinks/junctions can bypass it; (2) code duplication detection and egress screening both rely on undefined helper functions, risking silent failures.
risks: Symlink/junction bypass of path containment checks in both egress and worktree allocation
Undefined helper functions causing runtime errors in production paths
todos: Verify if screen_egress and allocate_worktree resolve symlinks before checking containment
Locate definitions of secret_floor_rule, _EGRESS_HINT, _strip_comments_generic, and ensure they are imported correctly

hypotheses.claim: Both egress screening (screen_egress) and worktree allocation (allocate_worktree) assume that lexical path checks are sufficient to prevent escape, but neither resolves symlinks/junctions, so an attacker can bypass containment by placing a symlink inside the allowed path.
hypotheses.mechanism: screen_egress checks channels/paths against a set of allowed patterns using lexical comparisons (no symlink resolution). allocate_worktree uses _lexical(root) and _is_within which compare paths lexically without resolving symlinks. If an attacker can create a symlink inside the allowed root that points outside, both checks pass but the actual I/O escapes.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Evidence that either screen_egress or allocate_worktree resolves symlinks (e.g., uses os.path.realpath) before performing containment checks.
evidence: daedalus/council/publish.py:screen_egress (lexical path check implied by docstring and lack of realpath mention)
daedalus/kairos/worktree.py:allocate_worktree (uses _is_within and _refuse_if_repo_adjacent with lexical paths, as noted in observations)

hypotheses.claim: Multiple critical functions across modules rely on undefined helper functions that are not defined or imported in the scanned chunks, raising the risk of NameError at runtime or silent fallback to incorrect behavior.
hypotheses.mechanism: screen_egress calls secret_floor_rule and uses _EGRESS_HINT, both undefined in its chunk. _generic_abstract_tokens calls _strip_comments_generic, which is also undefined. If these helpers are not provided via imports or definition in other chunks, the code will fail at runtime.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Evidence that the missing symbols are defined in other chunks of the same module or imported correctly (e.g., from a common utility module).
